title: Maderistas
capsule: The Maderistas were the revolutionary faction that coalesced around Francisco I. Madero during the 1910–1911 phase of the Mexican Revolution, drawing on rural insurgents led by Emiliano Zapata in Morelos and Pascual Orozco in Chihuahua. Their military campaign forced the resignation of Porfirio Díaz under the Treaty of Ciudad Juárez (21 May 1911), ending thirty-five years of the Porfiriato. Madero's election as president in November 1911 should have consolidated the movement, but his moderate programme alienated both Zapatista agrarians — who issued the Plan de Ayala in November 1911 denouncing him — and conservative Orozquistas who rebelled in 1912. The Maderista moment effectively closed when General Victoriano Huerta's coup and Madero's murder in February 1913 ended the constitutional experiment.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Maderistas were a diffuse political-military coalition rather than a bounded territory; their geographic extent fluctuates with campaign lines documented in contemporary press and administrative records, making exact mapping imprecise.
